Manager: Travis.
"TravDaddy," a member since 2013 and one of the finest managers the league has known. Three-time champion, back to back in 2016 and 2017, then again in 2021, when he ripped off ten straight weekly wins. A true believer in the strong pitching staff, built around Max Scherzer. His masterpiece: Trea Turner in the 23rd round of the 2016 draft.

The Commissioner. A founding member, the man the league is named for, and the standard every other manager is measured against. Eight-time champion (2009, 2010, 2013, 2015, 2019, 2024, 2025, 2026), including the league's first three-peat, 2024 through 2026. He has reached the playoffs 17 times in 17 seasons and finished first in the regular season 14 times. Once won 23 straight weekly matchups, from the start of 2017 into 2018. S&F Hall of Fame rules: players need 8 S&F seasons and 3 full seasons since their last; managers need 8 seasons and can go in while active; 100 computer voters (25 voting philosophies) name 3-5 each; 75 votes elects; under 5 votes or 10 years on the ballot comes off. Hall of Fame Day is November 1.
Members: 2020 Prince Fielder, Show, David Ortiz; 2021 Adrián González, Matt Holliday; 2022 Travis, Félix Hernández, José Bautista; 2023 Ryan Braun, Robinson Canó; 2024 Adrián Béltre; 2025 David Price; 2026 Albert Pujols, Adam Wainwright; 2027 Joey Votto, Zack Greinke, Miguel Cabrera
Voting philosophies: The Compilers (Career totals above all); The Peak Guys (Five great seasons beat fifteen good ones); The Ring Counters (Flags fly forever); The Small-Hall Purists (Only the inner circle); The Big-Hall Boosters (Let them in); The Statheads (Career and peak, nothing else); The Awards Voters (MVPs, Cy Youngs, Manager of the Year and league-best seasons); The Loyalty Voters (Keeper years, playoff habits and time served); Old School (Winners, awards and a long career); The Pitching Coaches (Lean toward arms); The Slugger's Friends (Lean toward bats); The First-Ballot Gatekeepers (Make first-timers wait unless they are obvious); The Longevity Voters (Seasons in S&F); Championship or Bust (Rings first, then peak); The JAWS Voters (Average of career and peak against the Hall standard); The Moderates (A bit of everything); The Patient Ones (Warm to a candidate each year he waits); The Contrarians (Have their own list); The Franchise Icon Voters (What he meant to one S&F team; for managers, the win-loss record); The Commissioner's Proxies (Balanced, slightly strict); The Skipper's Friends (Lean toward managers); The Players-Only Traditionalists (Never vote for a manager who is still managing); The Dynasty Voters (Titles and first-place finishes); The Analytics Interns (The Hall-standard number, strictly); The Nostalgists (A soft spot for the league's first years)

docs.t: S&F Gazette: Three in a row for The Show
docs.x:
The S&F Gazette, Monday, September 21, 2026 (The championship, covering Sept. 14–20). Headline: Three in a row for The Show. Show beats Preston 11-7 for his third straight title and his eighth since 2009, both league records.
Show is the champion again. He beat Preston 11-7 in the title game for his third straight championship and his eighth since 2009. No one else in the league has more than three.
He did it on 33.2 innings, just clear of the 30-inning minimum: a 3.21 ERA and a 1.16 WHIP against Preston’s 3.86 and 1.33. Show also scored 35 runs to 29, out-homered him 8-7 and got on base at .353 to .327. Preston took hits, RBI, steals, wins, strikeouts, K/9 and saves plus holds. It wasn’t enough.
It was the third title game between the two in five seasons. Preston won the first, 11-7 in 2022. Show has won the last two: 10-7 last year and 11-7 now.
The top seed had a bye, then beat Guy 13-4 in the semifinals with 14 homers and 10 steals. Preston, the 4 seed, earned his way: 13-2 over Travis, then 11-6 over Carter, the 2 seed, taking all nine hitting categories.
Champion: Show: 8 titles, 3 straight, and 24-11-1 in playoff categories.
Runner-up: Preston: in the final for the second straight year. Both times it was Show.
Third place: Guy: went from the 6 seed to third: 11-6 over Carter with a 1.09 ERA and a 0.94 WHIP.
Consolation: Mosby: won the consolation bracket, 10-7 over Paul.

docs.t: S&F Gazette: Guy steals the last seat
docs.x:
The S&F Gazette, Monday, August 31, 2026 (Final week of the regular season, covering Aug. 24–30). Headline: Guy steals the last seat. A 14-2 rout of Morgan and Mosby’s loss to Show flip sixth place in the season’s final week.
Mosby started the week holding the sixth and final playoff spot, seven category wins ahead of Guy. By Sunday night it belonged to somebody else.
Guy took 14 of 18 categories from Morgan behind a 1.25 ERA and 49 strikeouts in 36 innings. Across the league, Show beat Mosby 12-5. Add it up and Guy finishes 182-182-32, Mosby 180-184-32. Twenty-two weeks, and it came down to two wins.
Guy’s reward is a quarterfinal against Micah, who tuned up by beating Justin 15-3 and passed Travis for fourth on the way out the door.
Mosby’s reward is the consolation bracket and a long winter of looking at that pitching line: a 6.17 ERA and 22 walks in 35 innings.
Elsewhere, John closed out a lost season by taking 14 categories from Travis, who had already clinched and threw 27 innings all week.
Team of the week: Carter: would have beaten all 11 other teams: 39 runs, a 0.68 ERA and a 0.63 WHIP.
Bad beat: Preston: hit 12 homers, struck out 59 and would have beaten 10 teams. He drew the eleventh.
Got away with one: Show: posted a 5.00 ERA, would have lost to seven teams, and won 12-5.
Asleep at the wheel: Justin: (29.2 innings) and Travis (27.0) missed the 30-inning minimum and forfeited every pitching category.

docs.t: S&F Gazette: Crochet changes hands twice
docs.x:
The S&F Gazette, Monday, March 2, 2026 (monthly trade issue). Headline: Crochet changes hands twice. John bought him from Morgan on Feb. 19 and sold him to Paul a week later, the loudest of 13 trades in February.
February is when the 2026 off-season woke up. After one trade in December and none in January, 13 went through in 28 days, the most in a single month since February 2021.
John was in the middle of it. On Feb. 19 he sent four picks to Morgan for Garrett Crochet and four picks back. On Feb. 26 he flipped Crochet to Paul for 9.4, 12.7 and a 2027 10th-rounder, and graded on results he won that one 81-19. Crochet gave Paul 0.0 value points in 2026.
Preston made four deals and lost three of them on results. The one that stings: on Feb. 24 he sent Geraldo Perdomo, the best free-agent pickup in league history, and three picks to Morgan for 9.8, 14.8 and 22.5. Morgan wins it 74-26.
Carter's best work was his quietest. He gave Justin 12.8 for Ben Rice and 16.6 on Feb. 22. Rice gave him 13.4 value points, and Carter finished second.
Steal of the month: Morgan: graded 97-3 at the time and 74-26 on results for Perdomo.
Rough month: Paul: made three trades. None graded above 47 on results.
Even swap: Morgan and Show: traded Bo Naylor for Brett Baty on Feb. 20. Graded 50-50.

The Hot Take Desk is six made-up commentators: “Furnace” Frank Delvecchio, The spicy one: Yells about everything. Has never been wrong, according to him. ["Frank has called S&F games since the league's first Yahoo draft in 2009, and by his count he has been right about every single one. He has not.", 'He grades trades with his whole chest. A 20 is an insult to his family. A 4 is a crime scene. Anything over 90 gets a standing ovation from the only person in the studio, which is Frank.', 'Off the air, he still has the 2013 Billy Butler trade printed and taped to his dashboard. He reads it at red lights. "For motivation," he says.']; The Professor, Trades and drafts: Buries you with your own numbers. ['The Professor does not raise his voice. He raises a spreadsheet. He has value points for every player since 2009 and he will read them to you, slowly, until you agree with him.', 'His favorite thing in the world is a trade that looks fair and is not. His second favorite is explaining why, using the word "marginal" at least four times.', 'He has never once been asked to the cookout. He has a theory about why, and it has a regression line.']; Coach Skip, Weekly matchups: Hates spreadsheets. Thinks you lost because you did not want it. ["Coach Skip played a little, coached a lot, and trusts none of it that comes on a computer. Value points? He's got two: did you want it, and did you show up.", "He covers the weekly matchups, which means he spends Monday mornings telling the losers they lost because they did not want it bad enough. The math says otherwise. Skip says the math wasn't there.", 'He keeps sunflower seeds in every jacket he owns and has spit shells at three different producers.']; Dee from the Waiver Wire, Adds and drops: Treats every drop like a breakup. ['Dee lives on the waiver wire. Every add is a first date, every drop is a breakup, and every guy who gets cut and goes on a heater is the one that got away.', 'She has a box of tissues on the desk at all times and has needed it for nearly every Monday since 2009. She is still not over Todd Helton going unclaimed in 2009.', 'Her advice to every manager is the same: "Go back and check the wire. Somebody good is out there waiting for you."']; The Intern, Wild card: Terrified of Frank. Says the meanest thing by accident. ["The Intern got the job because nobody else answered the posting. He fetches Frank's coffee, holds Skip's seeds and reads the numbers off the cards the Professor hands him.", "He is scared of Frank, scared of the managers and a little scared of the Professor's spreadsheets. He is so nervous that the meanest thing said on the desk each week usually comes out of his mouth, by accident, in the nicest voice possible.", 'He would like everyone to know he is very sorry, and also that the grade really was a 2.']; Vinnie “The Spoon” Scarpelli, The instigator: Never has a take of his own. Repeats yours, louder, to the guy you said it about. ['Vinnie Scarpelli brings a wooden spoon to the desk every night because, in his words, somebody has to stir the pot. He has never had an opinion of his own. He takes yours, turns up the volume and reads it to the manager you said it about.', "Every segment he finds the two managers most likely to start something, reads one of them the other's numbers and asks the same question: “You gonna let him talk to you like that?” Then he leans back and lets the group chat do the rest.", "Frank thinks Vinnie is on his side. The Professor thinks Vinnie is on his side. Vinnie has never been on anybody's side. He keeps a second spoon in his jacket in case the first one breaks."]

docs.t: Hot Take Desk: The 2027 power rankings, with a new voice on the desk
docs.x:
Hot Take Desk segment "The 2027 power rankings, with a new voice on the desk" (Vinnie the Spoon's first night · Nov 16).
  Furnace Frank: Show won it all in 2026 and the projections put him 22.0 points clear of everybody for 2027. Juan Soto, Shohei Ohtani, Junior Caminero. That is not a keeper core. That is an ALL-STAR BALLOT!
  Vinnie the Spoon: Travis. Buddy. You're second, and Frank just said Show is 22.0 points clear of you. Twenty-two! Your eight keepers project to 76.7, his to 98.8. I'm not saying anything. I'm just saying the trade window opens December 1 and everybody's watching.
  The Professor: Carter finished second in 2026. His eight best keepers project to 54.1 value points, ninth in the league, and the best of them is Ben Rice at 10.1. The standings remember 2026. The projections do not.
  Vinnie the Spoon: Carter, you hear that? NINTH. The Professor called your keepers ninth, on the air, to your face, and you finished second! You gonna let a man with a spreadsheet talk to you like that? I'd be on the phone right now.
  Coach Skip: Justin went from 11th to 8th without playing a game. James Wood and Pete Crow-Armstrong, young legs. I like it. Now go win something.
  Dee: Paul is 12th of 12, and his best keeper is Steven Kwan at 9.2. Honey, Kwan is lovely, but he is not carrying a franchise. The trade window opens December 1.
  The Intern: Um, the picks aren't even. Morgan's 2027 picks are worth 42.7, the most in the league, and Micah's are worth 26.1, the least, because of trades made before this off-season. So the picks matter too. Sorry, Frank. Sorry, Vinnie. Please don't repeat that to Frank, Vinnie.

docs.t: League rules, Article I: The League
docs.x:
S&F rules, Article I, The League:
  1.1 Name: The league is the Showler & Friends Fantasy Baseball League (“S&F” or “the League”), hosted on Yahoo Fantasy Baseball as “S&F Baseball.”
  1.2 Membership: The League consists of twelve (12) managers, each holding one franchise.
  1.3 Free league: The League is a free league. No entry fee is collected and no prize money is paid. A February 2022 proposal to make S&F a money league received 7 votes for and 4 against and was not adopted; the League remained free.
  1.4 Official channels: League announcements, off-season trades, and votes are posted in the S&F Baseball Facebook group. The league website and the off-season rosters and draft boards it links to are the League’s record between seasons. Every manager is expected to follow the Facebook group.

S&F rules, Article II, Managers:
  2.1 Duties: Each manager shall check and set his lineup, make roster moves, be available for trade talks, and respond when contacted. A manager who can no longer meet these duties shall tell the Commissioner, who will find a replacement and may place the departing manager on a list for re-entry.
  2.2 Notice of resignation: A manager who intends to leave the League must notify the Commissioner before December 1 so a replacement can be in place before the off-season opens.
  2.3 Removal for inactivity: A franchise left unattended may be reassigned by the Commissioner to a new manager during the season. The first such reassignment took place in July 2014.
  2.4 Retention vote (the “3–3 Rule”): (a) A manager who finishes in the bottom three of the final regular-season standings in three consecutive seasons is placed before the League for a retention vote.
(b) Before the vote the Commissioner contacts the manager to confirm he wishes to continue. Each voting manager is then contacted privately; individual votes are confidential and only the totals are announced.
(c) The manager in question, the Commissioner, and any manager in his first season do not vote. A majority of the votes cast for removal removes the manager.
(d) A manager who is retained faces a new vote after each later season in which he again finishes in the bottom three. A finish outside the bottom three resets his count to zero.
(e) The Commissioner announces at the start of a season which managers are in an evaluation year.
  2.5 Co-managers: A manager may add a co-manager, subject to these conditions: (a) the co-manager is not added to the Facebook group or the league website; (b) all trade negotiations go through the head manager, and a co-manager who negotiates trades outside Yahoo is removed; (c) the co-manager may make transactions and send trade offers on Yahoo; (d) the Commissioner may remove a co-manager at any time.

docs.t: League rules, Article III: The Commissioner and Rulemaking
docs.x:
S&F rules, Article III, The Commissioner and Rulemaking:
  3.1 Authority: The Commissioner administers the League, enters keepers and off-season trades, sets the schedule and deadlines, and rules on every question these rules do not answer. Final decisions rest with the Commissioner.
  3.2 Recommendations: Any manager may propose a rule change. The Commissioner posts each recommendation to the Facebook group for discussion and, where he judges it warranted, a league vote. The Commissioner makes the final decision.
  3.3 When changes take effect: A rule change adopted during a season takes effect the following season or off-season unless the vote states that it takes effect immediately. Disputes over existing rules are raised privately with the Commissioner during the off-season, not in public during the season.
  3.4 Duty to verify: Each manager shall check his roster and draft board after every posted trade and before each draft, and report any error to the Commissioner.
  3.5 Rules Committee (inactive): From 2015 through the 2018–19 off-season, a three-member Rules Committee elected by the League for one-year terms beginning December 1 reviewed recommendations, with the Commissioner holding the final word. The committee did not rule on trades. It was discontinued beginning with the 2019–20 off-season, when recommendations moved to open league discussion under §3.2.

docs.t: League rules, Article IV: The League Year
docs.x:
S&F rules, Article IV, The League Year:
  4.1 Season designation: Each off-season belongs to the season that follows it. A trade made from December 1 through the keeper deadline is a trade of the following season (for example, December 1, 2025 to March 2026 is the 2026 season).
  4.2 Calendar: December 1 — Off-season opens; off-season trades may be submitted.
February — Annual Meeting (§4.3).
End of February — Keeper deadline (§7.3); the off-season closes.
Mid-March, Sunday — Draft.
August — Trade deadline (§9.7).
Second-to-last week of the MLB season — Championship ends (§11.4).
  4.3 Annual Meeting: The League holds an Annual Meeting each February, ordinarily on the last Sunday before the keeper deadline. The agenda includes the season awards, recommendation discussions, the division draft (§11.2), and trade talks. Managers who cannot attend should be reachable by phone during the meeting.

docs.t: League rules, Article V: Rosters and Lineups
docs.x:
S&F rules, Article V, Rosters and Lineups:
  5.1 Roster: Each team carries 26 roster spots: 16 starting spots and 10 bench spots. In addition each team has 5 injured-list (IL) spots and 2 minor-league (NA) spots.
  5.2 Starting lineup: C, 1B, 2B, 3B, SS, OF, OF, OF, Util; SP, SP, SP, RP, RP, P, P.
  5.3 NA eligibility: A player may occupy an NA spot only while Yahoo lists him as NA-eligible.
  5.4 Minimum innings: Each team must pitch at least 30 innings per weekly matchup. A team that falls short forfeits the pitching categories for that matchup.
  5.5 Off-season rosters: There is no roster limit during the off-season. Only the eight keepers (and NA keepers) carry into the new season.

S&F rules, Article VI, Scoring:
  6.1 Format: Head-to-head, by categories. Each category won is a win, each lost a loss, each tied a tie. Standings are by winning percentage.
  6.2 Hitting categories (9): Runs (R), Hits (H), Home Runs (HR), Runs Batted In (RBI), Stolen Bases (SB), Walks (BB), Strikeouts (K, fewer is better), Batting Average (AVG), On-Base Percentage (OBP).
  6.3 Pitching categories (9): Wins (W), Hits allowed (H), Walks allowed (BB), Strikeouts (K), ERA, WHIP, Strikeouts per nine innings (K/9), Blown Saves (BSV), Saves plus Holds (SV+H). Hits, walks, ERA, WHIP and blown saves are scored low.

S&F rules, Article VII, Keepers:
  7.1 Number: Each team keeps eight (8) players from its roster into the new season.
  7.2 NA keepers: In addition to the eight keepers, a team may keep up to two (2) minor-league-eligible players, defined as 151 or fewer major-league at-bats and 51 or fewer major-league innings pitched. NA keepers occupy the team’s 25th- and 26th-round picks. A team that keeps fewer than two uses the open round(s) in the draft.
  7.3 Deadline: Keepers are due to the Commissioner by 11:59 p.m. Central on the last day of February (midnight beginning March 1), unless the Commissioner announces a different deadline. Keepers are sent to the Commissioner by text or Facebook message with each player’s full name, and NA keepers designated as such.
  7.4 Early submission: A manager may submit keepers at any time before the deadline. Submitting keepers ends that manager’s off-season: he may make no further off-season trades.
  7.5 Failure to submit: If a manager has not submitted keepers by the deadline, the Commissioner sets that team’s keepers as the eight highest-ranked players on its roster by Yahoo’s O-Rank.
  7.6 Changing a keeper: Once submitted, a keeper may be replaced only if he suffers a significant injury, is suspended, retires, or meets a similar unexpected circumstance. The replacement must be requested before the draft, by the time the Commissioner sets on draft day. No keeper may be changed after the draft.

docs.t: League rules, Article VIII: The Draft
docs.x:
S&F rules, Article VIII, The Draft:
  8.1 Format: A live snake draft on Yahoo, held on a Sunday evening in mid-March, with one minute per pick. Keepers fill rounds 1 through 8, so the League’s first live round is the 9th.
  8.2 Rounds: The draft runs 26 rounds. Rounds 25 and 26 are reserved for NA keepers (§7.2) and may not be traded.
  8.3 Draft order: Draft order is the reverse of final regular-season winning percentage across all twelve teams, regardless of division titles or postseason results. The team with the worst record picks first.
  8.4 Draft lottery (repealed): A weighted lottery among non-playoff teams, with bonus chances for the top three consolation finishers, was adopted by league vote in February 2018 and used for the 2019 draft. It was repealed in 2019 and replaced by the consolation champion’s division pick (§11.5).

S&F rules, Article IX, Trades:
  9.1 What may be traded: Players and draft picks may be traded. A player may be traded in the off-season only if he was on the team’s final roster. Trades may involve any number of teams.
  9.2 Draft picks: Picks in the next two drafts may be traded. Each side of a trade must receive the same number of draft picks it gives up. Rounds 25 and 26 may not be traded (§8.2).
  9.3 Off-season trades: From December 1 until his keeper submission, a manager may trade by agreement with another manager. Both managers (every manager, in a multi-team trade) must send the Commissioner the exact same trade, naming each draft pick by round and pick number. The trade becomes official when the Commissioner posts it to the Facebook group and updates the off-season rosters and draft boards.
  9.4 Entering off-season pick trades: Off-season trades of picks in the current draft are entered on Yahoo before the draft. Off-season trades of picks in the following year’s draft are re-entered on Yahoo after the draft, once that draft board opens.
  9.5 In-season trades: In-season trades are made on Yahoo.
  9.6 Veto: Any manager may vote on Yahoo to veto an accepted in-season trade within one day. Seven (7) veto votes reject the trade. A trade that does not reach seven votes processes automatically.
  9.7 Trade deadline: The in-season trade deadline falls in August on the date the Commissioner sets on Yahoo (August 6 in 2026).
  9.8 Negotiation courtesy: A manager who declines an offer should say why, or counter it, so the other manager knows whether to try again.

S&F rules, Article X, Transactions:
  10.1 Free agents and waivers: Free agents may be added at any time, with no limit on acquisitions per week or per season. Dropped players clear waivers in two days; waiver priority is a continual rolling list.
  10.2 Lineup timing: Lineup changes take effect the same day (Yahoo “Daily – Today”): a player may be started until his game begins.
  10.3 Mistakes: Each manager is responsible for his own transactions. A roster move made in error stands.

docs.t: League rules, Article XI: Divisions, Schedule and Postseason
docs.x:
S&F rules, Article XI, Divisions, Schedule and Postseason:
  11.1 Divisions: The League plays in three divisions of four teams, redrawn every year.
  11.2 Division draft: At the Annual Meeting the previous season’s champion, runner-up and third-place finisher each lead a division and draft its members in that order, snaking, for three rounds. Each leader names his division.
  11.3 Schedule: Each team plays its three division opponents four times each and every other team at least once; the remaining weeks are additional non-division matchups. The All-Star break week is combined with the next week into a single matchup.
  11.4 Playoffs: Six teams qualify. The three division winners receive the top three seeds; the remaining three spots go to the best records. The top two seeds receive a first-round bye, and teams are reseeded after each round. The playoffs run three weeks, ending with the championship in the second-to-last week of the MLB season. A third-place game is played.
  11.5 Consolation tournament: The six non-playoff teams play a consolation tournament. The consolation champion chooses which division he joins for the next season, taking his place at the start of the third round of the division draft in place of the third-round pick of the division he chooses.
  11.6 Tiebreaker: A tied playoff or consolation matchup is decided by the regular-season results between the two teams, counted in total categories won. If still tied, the higher seed advances.
  11.7 Honors: The champion receives the S&F championship banner.

S&F rules, Article XII, Conduct:
  12.1 Sportsmanship: Trash talk is welcome. Personal put-downs are not. Once a rule is applied or a vote is decided, managers accept the result and move on.

docs.t: League rules, Article XIII: Interrupted Seasons
docs.x:
S&F rules, Article XIII, Interrupted Seasons:
  13.1 Shortened MLB seasons: When MLB cancels games, the League cancels the fantasy matchups covering the same dates.
  13.2 Cancelled seasons: If a season cannot be played, rosters and draft boards carry over unchanged into the next off-season. The 2020 season was cancelled under this rule; the 2020 draft was never held, and any 2020 games played were an unofficial redraft.

The Showler and Friends Fantasy Baseball League was created in 2009. It started as a casual, fun league with friends; it quickly evolved into a competitive keeper league. Beginning with six keepers going into the 2010 season, each manager now keeps eight players from their squad, which started in 2011. Most of the league's managers are from Oklahoma, with two residing in Oregon. The league does not play for money but rather the right to boast in whatever way the manager feels the need. This league uses Yahoo Fantasy Baseball, which the commish found as the best site for fantasy sports. From the league opening date in late January to the close in October, the league uses the Yahoo site to play the game. The league, however, doesn't stop there. Starting December 1st, the managers will take their final rosters and prepare for the Off-Season. During the Off-Season, managers may trade from their final roster and draft picks in the next year's draft. This is where the managers build their rosters and use their philosophy to prepare for the following year or years based on the players obtained. Each year, the league holds a fantasy meeting to discuss trades, talk strategies, and hold the division draft, with the top three teams picking who will be in their division for the upcoming season. The suggestion committee will also release their rulings on the suggestions from the league.
